news.headline: 360-Degree AI Implementation: Empowering Student Learning, Preserving Academic Integrity and Boosting Operational Efficiencies
AI 101: Workbook for Teachers and School Leaders
Creating Effective AI Policies: A Guide for Educators

paragraphs: BrainFreeze sells an artificial intelligence platform aimed at everyone in a school district. Teachers get lesson planning, automated grading, and content creation. Students get tutoring, writing assistance, and homework help around the clock in more than a hundred languages. Administrators oversee district-wide rollout with security controls and central management tools.

Districts can start with prepared assistants for lesson planning, grading, and student support. They can upload curriculum materials so assistants reference their own content. A drag-and-drop builder lets staff make custom tools without programming. The platform connects to a district's existing LMS, SIS, Google Workspace, and Microsoft 365. Students can be invited into controlled virtual environments where they use AI without personal accounts.

The company says the platform meets FERPA, COPPA, and GDPR requirements and holds SOC 2 and ISO certifications. It states that AI providers are not permitted to train on student data. For schools in the United States it leans on the Access 4 Learning Community's National Data Privacy Agreement. A data loss prevention layer monitors, blocks, or redacts sensitive data before it reaches AI models.
